title: Docker Local Development Architecture
purpose: Show the local docker-compose up development architecture with frontend and backend containers, their configurations, and external cloud service dependencies.
audience: Developers, DevOps engineers, new team members setting up local environment
description: Local development environment started via docker-compose up. Frontend container (podm-frontend) runs Node 18 Alpine with Vite Dev Server on port 5173, mounts source code for hot reload, and proxies API requests to the backend. Backend container (PoDM_project) runs Node 18 Alpine with ts-node-dev on port 5000, mounts source code for hot reload, and connects to external cloud services: Supabase PostgreSQL (remote), Cloudflare R2 Storage, Ethereum RPC (Base network), and OpenAI/OpenRouter API. No local PostgreSQL or Nginx — all persistent services are remote. The Vite dev proxy handles routing in development mode. Frontend runs npm run dev (not production build).

File uploads and signed URL generation fail

API requests from frontend 404 or fail to reach backend

validationRules: Frontend requires VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY env vars
Backend requires SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, R2 credentials, Stripe keys, and RPC_URL env vars
Docker Compose depends on docker-compose.yml in project root
securityConsiderations: SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY in backend .env provides full database access — must be kept secure
Stripe secret keys in backend .env must not be exposed
No local database means development traffic hits production-adjacent Supabase instance
AI caption images sent to external API (OpenAI/OpenRouter) without explicit user consent
performanceConsiderations: Remote database adds network latency compared to local PostgreSQL
Hot reload with source mounts may be slower on macOS/Windows (Docker filesystem overhead)
ts-node-dev recompiles TypeScript on every change — slower than production builds
